memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living creature I have made." - Gen 7:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the first drop of rain fell, God told Noah exactly what was coming: "Seven days from now I will send rain." God does not act in the dark. He warned Noah, gave him time to prepare, and even set a precise timetable. This is the character of God throughout Scripture - He warns before He judges, always giving space and opportunity before the storm breaks.

Think of those seven final days. A whole week of grace, of last chances, while Noah and his family gathered into the ark. God is patient right up to the end, "not wanting anyone to perish, but everyone to come to repentance" (2 Pet 3:9). Even as judgement approached, God's mercy was still at work, still counting down with kindness.

This tells us something important about God. He is not eager to judge. He is slow to anger, quick to warn, generous with time. Every warning in Scripture is itself an act of mercy - a loving voice saying, "Turn, before it is too late."

The same God warns us today, lovingly, through His Word. He tells us plainly of a coming day of judgement, not to frighten us, but to draw us to safety in Christ before that day comes. The warning is the mercy. Do not treat God's warnings as threats to resent, but as the loving voice of a God who wants you safe. Today, while there is still time, come into the ark of His salvation.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you hear God's warnings as threats, or as loving mercy?
- Is there a warning from God's Word you need to heed today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Merciful God, thank You that You always warn before You act, giving time to turn to You. Help me hear Your warnings as loving mercy, and to take refuge in Christ while there is still time.
